title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the P.S. of the 1965 letter. The P.S. describes 'the modular varieties one gets from motive-theoretic Galois theory'.

Set-up from the previous page, in modern terms:
- G is a connected reductive Q-group.
- U_R is the circle S^1 = Res_{C/R}G_m^{norm=1}.
- i_0 : U_R -> G_R is a homomorphism with i_0(-1) central (a weight condition), such that the centralizer K_R of i_0(sqrt(-1)) has maximal compact identity component. In Deligne's language, Ad i_0(i) is a Cartan involution.
- i_0 is non-trivial on every R-simple factor.
- C_R = Cent(i_0) ⊂ K_R, and Q̌ = G_R/C_R.
- 𝒱 = G(R)^0/(G(R)^0 ∩ C(R)) is a homogeneous complex manifold. In modern terms it is a Mumford–Tate domain / Griffiths–Schmid period (flag) domain D = G(R)^+/H, with H the compact centralizer of a circle.

Every Q-representation V of G with a lattice V_0 gives a holomorphic family of Q-Hodge structures on 𝒱. Over C, i_0 gives the bigrading V^{p,q}, and the total degree n is fixed by requiring i_0(-1) to act on V as the homothety (-1)^n. The family is polarizable if one chooses a G-invariant form φ.

The parenthetical gives a Tannakian description. 𝒱 represents a functor F on complex-analytic spaces X: F(X) is the set of ways of attaching to every representation V, additively and multiplicatively (i.e. as an exact ⊗-functor), a holomorphic family of Hodge structures on X. This is the 'moduli of ⊗-functors Rep(G) -> Hodge structures of given type' description of a Mumford–Tate domain. Note there is no Griffiths transversality: the families are holomorphic but not horizontal.

Let Γ be the stabilizer of V_0. Then Γ acts on the pair (𝒱, family of Hodge structures).

Conjecture (boxed): for Γ ⊂ G(Q) ∩ G(R)^0 commensurable with G(Z) (an arithmetic subgroup), the quotient 𝒱/Γ should carry an algebraic structure over Q, and usually over Z. Grothendieck hedges that extra conditions might be needed:
- arithmetic ones: existence of 'Frobenius elements' in I(Q), with I = G/int.aut., i.e. the adjoint group;
- geometric ones: e.g. G_R has no compact factor.

Margin note: in general 𝒱 is not Riemannian symmetric. It fibres over the symmetric space G(R)^0/K(R)^0, with fibres K/C that are projective complex homogeneous spaces under K_C. Hence 𝒱 is simply connected (contractible base, simply connected flag-variety fibres), and it is the universal cover of M = 𝒱/Γ when Γ acts freely.

The next page specializes to G = SO(φ) (or the symplectic group): Griffiths-type period domains of polarized Hodge structures with fixed Hodge numbers, generalizing the Siegel half-space.

Purpose: to locate the natural 'modular varieties' attached to (motivic) Galois groups of motives, as moduli of motives with given Galois group and Hodge type. This is essentially the notion of a Shimura datum / Mumford–Tate domain, written before Mumford (1966), Griffiths (1968) and Deligne (1971).
errors: The complex structure of 𝒱 is said to be 'inherited from one on Q̌(R)'. Q̌(R) = (G_R/C_R)(R) is a real manifold with no complex structure in general. The complex structure comes from the Borel-type open embedding G(R)^0/C(R) ⊂ G(C)/P(C), the compact dual flag variety, with P the parabolic defined by the Hodge filtration. 'open in Q̌(R)' is correct only as an open embedding of real manifolds.

The boxed algebraicity expectation is false in the stated generality. Without Deligne's condition that Ad∘i_0 has only Hodge types (-1,1),(0,0),(1,-1) (equivalently 𝒱 Hermitian symmetric, with horizontal = holomorphic), quotients Γ\𝒱 of non-classical period/flag domains admit no algebraic structure (Carlson–Toledo; Griffiths–Robles–Toledo 2014). Grothendieck's hedge ('extra conditions ... geometric') points the right way, but the decisive condition is transversality / Hermitian type, not 'no compact factor'.
'Algebraic structure over Q' is too strong in general. Canonical models of Shimura varieties are defined over the reflex field E(G,X), not Q, though the Siegel case is over Q.

The universal property, as stated (holomorphic ⊗-families of Hodge structures), describes 𝒱 correctly. But such non-horizontal families do not arise from geometry. Geometric variations satisfy Griffiths transversality, which Grothendieck does not mention.
On the next page G = SO(φ) is written for both the symmetric and the alternating case. For alternating φ it should be Sp(φ).
Γ is first introduced as a subgroup of G(R). For an arithmetic quotient it should be in G(Q), as corrected later on the page.

ideas.what: Datum (G reductive over Q, i_0: S^1 -> G_R with i_0(-1) central, Ad i_0(i) a Cartan involution, non-trivial on simple factors) defining a homogeneous complex domain G(R)^0/Cent(i_0)
ideas.modern_name: Shimura datum / Mumford–Tate domain (Hodge datum), period domain as G(R)/H
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Travaux de Shimura, 1971; Variétés de Shimura, 1979); Mumford (1966) for Hodge/Mumford–Tate groups; Griffiths–Schmid (1969) for homogeneous period domains
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA. Possibly echoed in the Grothendieck–Serre correspondence (1964 letters on motives), but this exact formulation is unsure.

ideas.what: 𝒱 represents the functor of exact ⊗-functors Rep_Q(G) -> holomorphic families of Hodge structures on X
ideas.modern_name: Tannakian description of Mumford–Tate domains / moduli of G-Hodge structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne; Green–Griffiths–Kerr (Mumford–Tate domains, 2012); Tannakian formalism by Saavedra (1972)

ideas.what: Fibration of 𝒱 over the Riemannian symmetric space G/K with compact projective homogeneous fibres K/C, hence 𝒱 is simply connected
ideas.modern_name: Fibration D -> G(R)/K of a period domain over its symmetric space

ideas.what: Conjecture that arithmetic quotients 𝒱/Γ are algebraic, defined over Q and even over Z, possibly under extra arithmetic ('Frobenius elements in the adjoint group') or geometric conditions
ideas.modern_name: Canonical (integral) models of Shimura varieties; algebraicity question for Γ\D
ideas.usually_credited_to: Shimura, Deligne, Milne, Borovoi (canonical models); Kisin, Vasiu (integral models); Griffiths–Robles–Toledo (non-algebraicity in the non-classical case)

ideas.what: Viewing these quotients as moduli of motives with prescribed motivic Galois group and Hodge type
ideas.modern_name: Shimura varieties as moduli of motives (Deligne's motivic interpretation, Milne's conjecture)

missed.claim: Historical priority. In 1965 Grothendieck wrote down essentially Deligne's axioms for a Shimura datum, including the Cartan-involution and simple-factor conditions, but with Cent(i_0) in place of K. This yields general Mumford–Tate/period domains, including their fibration over G/K. He also gave a Tannakian universal property and conjectured algebraicity over Q/Z of arithmetic quotients. This predates Mumford 1966, Griffiths 1968 and Deligne 1971, and is not usually credited to him.
missed.quote: The modular varieties I expect to carry algebraic structures over Q (and usually, Z) are the varieties 𝒱/Γ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that the motivic-Galois route to Shimura varieties and period domains originates with Grothendieck in 1965. This is relevant to the history of Deligne's 1971/1979 formalism.

missed.claim: The suggested arithmetic condition, existence of 'Frobenius elements' in the adjoint group I(Q), as a criterion for when 𝒱/Γ is an algebraic moduli space of motives. It was never developed. It loosely anticipates the role of special/CM points and Frobenius tori in canonical models and Langlands–Rapoport-type descriptions, but in this form it does not appear in the literature.
missed.quote: arithmetic (involving existence of "Frobenius elements" in I(Q), I = G/int. aut.)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests an arithmetic rather than Hodge-theoretic criterion for which Mumford–Tate domains admit algebraic, motivic moduli interpretations. This is a question still alive for non-classical domains, where Γ\D is not algebraic.

deep.surprise_reason: The datum anticipates Shimura data and Mumford–Tate domains, together with a Tannakian moduli interpretation, years before Mumford, Griffiths and Deligne. That is a notable and probably uncredited historical detail. However, the main conjecture is known to fail without the transversality / Hermitian condition, and the ideas are now standard.
transcription_corrections: 'I = G/inat. aut.' should read 'I = G/int. aut.' (inner automorphisms, i.e. the adjoint group).
'(𝒱, 𝒱)': the second symbol is the family of Hodge structures; Γ operates on the pair (domain, family).
Margin: 'projective complex Kähler [?] homogeneous spaces' should most likely read 'projective complex K_C-homogeneous spaces'. The fibres K/C are homogeneous under the complexification K_C.
Margin last line: 'if Γ operates freely' appears correct; the uncertain word likely reads 'freely'.
'homothety' is inserted above the line before '(-1)^n'.
'[-is-]': the first deleted word is an illegible scribble rather than 'is'.
